question: Using determinants, find the area of $\triangle PQR$ with vertices $P(3,1)$, $Q(9,3)$ and $R(5,7)$. Also, find the equation of line PQ using determinants.
explanation:
**Step 1:** Set up the determinant for the area of the triangle: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 3 & 1 \\ 5 & 7 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$$

**Step 2:** Expand the determinant along the first row: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \left| 3(3 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 7) - 1(9 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 5) + 1(9 \cdot 7 - 3 \cdot 5) \right|$$ $$= \frac{1}{2} \left| 3(3-7) - 1(9-5) + 1(63-15) \right|$$ $$= \frac{1}{2} \left| 3(-4) - 4 + 48 \right|$$

**Step 3:** Calculate the final area value: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \left| -12 - 4 + 48 \right| = \frac{1}{2} \left| 32 \right| = 16 \text{ sq. units}$$

**Step 4:** Set up the determinant for the equation of line PQ: $$\begin{vmatrix} x & y & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$$

**Step 5:** Expand along the first row to find the equation: $$x(1 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 3) - y(3 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 9) + 1(3 \cdot 3 - 1 \cdot 9) = 0$$ $$x(1-3) - y(3-9) + (9-9) = 0$$ $$-2x + 6y + 0 = 0 \Rightarrow -2x + 6y = 0$$ $$x - 3y = 0$$
